title: Propagation sidecar
description: Schema for .propagates.yml sidecars. Each sidecar covers the docs/CLAUDE.mds in its directory and declares where edits propagate.

workspace.description: This dir is a ledger-owning workspace root, not just an edge sidecar.

path.description: Relative path from this sidecar to the downstream file. May be a glob (e.g. `style/pages/**/*.md`) — the watcher fs-expands it and records a single summary entry {glob_matched, sample}; `doctor` requires ≥1 match. Must not be empty and must not end in '/' — a bare directory is never a valid downstream (reading it as content fails with EISDIR); declare a file or a glob instead. Schema cannot detect a directory that lacks a trailing slash — that check runs at doctor/validate time against the filesystem (see `classifyDownstreamPath` in cli.mjs).

why.description: Short reason this downstream depends on the source.

exclude.description: Only valid when `path` is a glob. Paths or globs (relative to this sidecar, resolved like `path`) that the glob matches but that must NOT be watched — e.g. pointer stubs (`# GOTCHAS.md — moved`) whose real file is already covered by another declaration. An excluded file mints no edge, and the remaining edges keep their ids. `doctor` FAILS on `exclude` with a literal `path`, and on an entry that matches none of the glob's matches (a stale exemption that can no longer fire). If every match is excluded the glob reports UNMATCHED. This, not `verify --disposition decoupled`, is how to drop one file from a glob: `decoupled` on a glob match is refused (N118).

authority.description: This SOURCE governs the downstream, beyond merely coupling to it. counsel = the source is the authority and its wording is not to be changed by whoever edits the downstream (legal copy, pricing); the edit-time hook BLOCKS. spec = the source defines intended behaviour; advisory. reference = useful background; advisory. Omit for an ordinary drift edge.

concepts.description: Forward-compat: per-section concept tags for graph-augment (V2). Keys are section anchors; values are concept candidate lists.
